fused_findings: agenttop is a lower-privilege OTLP-native observer whose main semantic evidence comes from provider-emitted logs/metrics plus local scraping; it is not an independent system-boundary witness.
agenttop's current /v1/traces handler accepts trace payloads but does not store or process them, so it does not presently close F2 causal trace requirements.
AgentSight is heavier and privilege/privacy sensitive but can independently observe process/file/network/resource behavior and therefore can disagree with application self-report.
The candidates are complementary, not interchangeable: routine low-friction OTLP observation and controlled independent system-witness falsification solve different epistemic problems.
A full agenttop import is not justified merely to receive OTLP; a thin F2-native standards-based ingress is the preferred E2 distillation direction.
Neither observer may mint UnifiedDB truth, EffectGate/EffectJournal outcome, completion evidence, or synthesize missing F2 causal_id/generation/effect_id from time/PID/session/tool identifiers.

proposed_pattern.tier_0: F2 typed telemetry + UnifiedDB evidence + EffectGate/EffectJournal authority
proposed_pattern.tier_1: minimal content-minimized F2-native OTLP ingress for provider-emitted telemetry
proposed_pattern.tier_2: pinned AgentSight sidecar/offline witness only for controlled diagnostic/falsification runs

next_discriminator: E3 deterministic secret-free OTLP fixture on an admitted FREE isolated surface, measuring exact field preservation, UNKNOWN-id preservation, replay/duplicate behavior, malformed/partial payload handling, redaction, and overhead; AgentSight independent-system A/B remains separate and later.
